$description: Declarative source for the Tier-3 Action matrix. Expanded into DTCG tokens by build/generate-component-tokens.mjs — NEVER hand-write the resulting token names. Spec §7.3.
$notes: Ramp steps, not filter: brightness(). button.css currently computes hover/active with
filter: brightness(0.95) — which means those colours cannot be contrast-tested, cannot be
expressed as Figma variables, and drift unpredictably under dark/HC themes. Naming the
step makes each state a designed, testable value.
`success` is an intent here but not in UX4G's Action matrix. SAMAVESH's Button ships one,
so the matrix describes the component we have (spec §7.3, corrected by the Phase 1 slice).

$stepNotes.fill: 600 not 500 — 500 fails 4.5:1 against white for the label on several ramps. See test/prominence-contract.test.mjs.
$stepNotes.disabled: A flat neutral fill, NOT the intent colour at reduced opacity: a washed-out red still reads as an error affordance.

$overrideNotes: Per-intent step overrides. The four ramps are NOT perceptually equivalent at equal steps,
so one step table cannot serve all of them. Entries here are found by
REMOVED 2026-08-11 — the whole `destructive` block, because the defect it worked around is
gone. It read: white on dangerScale.600 (#d64539) is 4.40:1, just under AA, so the filled
progression shifts up one step to 700/800/900; and dangerScale.800 on 200 is 4.02:1, so
the tonal hover text shifts to 900. Both were symptoms of a danger ramp anchored at the
wrong rung — #ec5042 is L* 64, inside the dead zone where no ink reaches 4.5:1. Re-anchored
at 400 (see build/brand-ramps.mjs) the same rungs measure 6.68:1 and 6.10:1, so destructive
now uses the SAME step table as every other intent, which is what a shared table is for.
A workaround kept past its cause is just an inconsistency nobody can explain.
brand/tonal/* — added 2026-08-11 with the regenerated ramps. The Navy brand runs DARKER
than Blue by design (the two are only 9 degrees apart in hue, so lightness is the only
thing telling them apart), which makes primaryScale.300 a MID tone in Navy rather than a
tint: navy 900 on navy 300 measured 4.33:1. The tonal progression therefore shifts down a
step to 50/100/200 for the brand intent only — the other three ramps are brand-invariant
$inverseNotes: For a button sitting on a solid brand surface (e.g. a navy page header). Modelled as a
qualifier so it composes with the variants above instead of needing new variant words.
Values are white-alpha, so they work on ANY solid surface rather than assuming navy.
